answers.question: If I wanted to add a new payment mode in the billing system, which files across the repositories would I need to touch?

paragraphs.text: Short answer: "payment mode" (cash, credit card, mobile money…) is a **data record**, not an enum. Adding a new one is normally just configuration done through the admin UI — you do **not** need to change code. You only touch code if you want to hard-code a mode, change the mode's fields, or give it extra input fields (attribute types).
Below is the picture, repository by repository.
## The core idea: payment modes are database rows

A `PaymentMode` is a metadata entity stored in the `cashier_payment_mode` table, with a name, description and sort order [1]. It is a normal OpenMRS metadata type (creator, dateCreated, retired, uuid), so it can be created, edited, retired or purged at runtime. That is why the O3 admin screen "Payment modes configuration" can add a new one without a code change.

Payment modes are referenced by two other things:
- A **service price** (the price of a billable service) points at one payment mode, so the same service can cost different amounts per mode [2].
- A **payment** records which mode it was made with — internally `Payment.instanceType` is a `PaymentMode` [3].
## If you only want to use a new mode (no code)
Add it in the UI at **Billing settings → Payment modes configuration**, then attach it to service prices in the billable-service form. The path is:

```mermaid
---
title: Adding a payment mode through the UI
---
flowchart TD
  page["Payment modes config page"] --> addBtn["Add new payment mode"]
  addBtn --> modal["Payment mode form modal"]
  modal --> resource["createPaymentMode"]
  resource --> rest["POST billing/paymentMode"]
  rest --> service["PaymentModeServiceImpl"]
  service --> db["cashier_payment_mode table"]
```

- The list page `PaymentModesConfig` reads modes with `usePaymentModes`, and its buttons open the add/edit and delete modals [4].
- `PaymentModeFormModal` validates name + description and calls `createPaymentMode` or `updatePaymentMode` [5].
- Those helpers do the real HTTP: `POST {restBaseUrl}/billing/paymentMode` and `POST {restBaseUrl}/billing/paymentMode/{uuid}` [6].
- On the server, `PaymentModeResource` exposes that REST endpoint and delegates to `PaymentModeService` [7], implemented by `PaymentModeServiceImpl`, which is wired to the Hibernate DAO in Spring [8].
## If you want a new mode to be pre-seeded or hard-coded

There is no enum or constant list of modes in either repository — I searched both and found only the entity, its service, its REST resource and UI code. So there is no single "add your mode here" list to edit. If your fork needs a mode guaranteed to exist on a fresh database, you would add it either:
- as **Liquibase seed data** in the module's changeset file, which already contains similar seed rows (for example the payments-by-payment-mode report property) [9] ; or
- as a small `PaymentMode` row created by the module activator.
I could not verify an existing payment-mode seed changeset — I only read the surrounding property-migration lines, not the whole file.
## If the new mode needs extra fields (attribute types)

Some modes need more data than an amount, e.g. a card transaction number. That is modelled as a `PaymentModeAttributeType`, owned by the payment mode [10], and a mode can build one via `addAttributeType(name, format, regExp, required)` [11]. It is persisted as a child list of the mode [12].

Relevant files if you extend this:
- `PaymentModeAttributeTypeResource` — REST CRUD for the attribute types [13].
- `PaymentAttributeResource` — the *values* captured for a payment [14].
- The legacy fragment controller that renders them [15].
- `IPaymentModeAttributeTypeService` / `PaymentModeAttributeTypeServiceImpl`, registered as a module service [16].

The O3 React form does **not** currently render payment-mode attribute types: `payment-mode-form.modal.tsx` only has name and description [17]. So a custom attribute would today only be usable through the legacy UI unless you extend that modal.
## Frontend files you'd touch for a code change

| Concern | File |
|---|---|
| Admin list page and routes into modals | [4] |
| Add/Edit modal (fields, validation) | [18] |
| Delete modal | [19] |
| Fetch hook + create/update calls | [20] |
| Pick a mode when taking a payment | [21] |
| Second fetch hook used by the invoice screen | [22] |
| Choosing mode per price in a service | [23] |
| TypeScript types for the API payloads | [24] |
| Component registration (ESM scripts) | [25] |
| Modal names → components | [26] |
| Settings menu entry | [27] |
| Route to the config page | [28] |
| Translations for any new label | [29] |
## Backend files you'd touch for a code change

- Entity: [30]
- Service interface / impl: [31] and [32]
- DAO: `PaymentModeDAO` with a Hibernate implementation registered as `HibernatePaymentModeDAOImpl` [33]
- REST resource: [34] — note the representation lists only `uuid, name, description, retired, retireReason, sortOrder, attributeTypes` [35], so a **new column on the mode needs a matching `addProperty` here** or the ESM never sees it.
- Hibernate mapping: [1]
- Billable-service mapper that resolves the selected mode UUID to a `PaymentMode` [36]
## Not involved

- **`openmrs-module-fhir2`**, **`openmrs-esm-form-engine-lib`**, **`openmrs-esm-patient-management`**: no matches for payment mode anywhere — the first is a FHIR API module, the other two are form/patient apps. Confirmed by a repository-wide search for `paymentMode|PaymentMode` that only returned matches in the billing module and billing app.
- **`openmrs-contrib-o3-docs`**: grep for payment mode there returned nothing, so no documentation page needs updating in this repo.
## What I could not verify

- Whether the module ships a Liquibase changeset that seeds default modes — I read only lines 951-952 of `liquibase.xml`, not the whole file.
- The default privilege wiring for creating modes; the module defines metadata privileges (`MANAGE_METADATA`, `PURGE_METADATA`) [37], but I did not trace which one `PaymentModeResource` actually enforces.
